lesson_title: Your City Is a Storage Heater
hook_text: Touch a brick wall an hour after sunset. Still warm. Your whole city does that — here's why it matters.
clip_script: Touch a face-brick wall an hour after sunset: still warm, like a loaf out of the oven. Touch a fence post on the farm at the same hour: cold. Cities are built almost entirely out of the warm-wall kind of stuff. Think of an old storage heater — the kind that quietly charges up all day and then glows warm all evening. A city is a storage heater the size of a municipality. From sunrise to sunset the dark tar, brick and concrete drink radiation; from sunset to sunrise they breathe it back into the streets. The city, though, cannot sweat. Its rain is rushed off roofs, down gutters, into drains and gone — so the sun's whole allowance is spent on heat.
visual_style: Thermal-camera aesthetic: a hand touching a glowing orange brick wall at dusk, split-screen with a cool blue farm fence, zooming out to a whole city glowing warm against dark countryside, one cool green patch over each park.
mood: Everyday-mystery revealed, warm and a little eerie.
pacing: Slow tactile open, steady zoom-out build, punchy park-dip payoff.
